verses.verse:
दक्षिणांगुलिभि स्तृाणि तृीणि बामांगुलीयकैः।
प्राच्छादनं तु छिद्राणाम् षट् स्वरायाम् प्रकल्पितम्।७४।
verses.text: Three [holes] with the fingers of the right [hand], three with the fingers of the left: this is the covering of the holes laid down for the ṣaṭsvarā (six-note flute).

commentary.text: That is, if the flute has six holes, the three upper holes should be closed with three fingers of the right hand, and the three lower holes with three fingers of the left hand. Keep in mind that the fingers should be as straight as possible, because if they are bent, success in practising the komal notes will later be hard to achieve. If the middle part of the middle finger is on the hole, the other two fingers will straighten by themselves. But if the flute is large, the fingers have to be slanted somewhat because of the distance between the holes. Even then, no finger should be raised in the middle and bent at the tip. It will be better if this too is done under a guru's guidance. Otherwise many kinds of faults and doubts will unsettle the practitioner. Now the placement of the fingers on nine holes is described.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
